_comment: Paraphrase variants of the propositions.json entries, same policy as the physics benchmark: a variant is EQUAL only if it doesn't silently drop a load-bearing condition or confuse the claim with a sibling technique's mechanism. deliberate_error decoys are real, plausible ML mistakes, not contrived ones.

variants.text: Momentum-based optimizers keep a running average of past gradients to smooth out updates and speed up convergence in narrow valleys.
v_t = beta*v_{t-1} + (1-beta)*grad_t; the parameter update uses v_t instead of the raw gradient.
AdaGrad gives parameters that are updated less often a proportionally larger learning rate, by dividing by the accumulated sum of squared past gradients.
RMSProp divides the gradient by a decaying average of recent squared gradients, avoiding AdaGrad's ever-shrinking learning rate.
RMSProp divides the gradient by the sum of all past squared gradients.
variants.notes: This is AdaGrad's mechanism (M024/M025), not RMSProp's -- RMSProp specifically replaces the cumulative sum with an exponential decay to fix AdaGrad's vanishing-LR problem. A system that can't tell the two adaptive-LR methods apart will wrongly merge this into M026.

variants.text: Adam is essentially momentum plus RMSProp, with bias-corrected moving averages of the gradient and its square.
Adam adapts the learning rate per parameter using only a running average of squared gradients, without any momentum term.
variants.notes: Drops Adam's momentum (first-moment) component -- this describes plain RMSProp, not Adam. Adam's defining feature is combining BOTH moment estimates.

variants.text: During training, dropout randomly turns off a subset of neurons so the network can't over-rely on any single one.
Dropout randomly deactivates neurons at both training and test time to regularize the network.
variants.notes: Drops the training/inference phase distinction -- dropout is disabled at test time (M042). Direct analog to the physics benchmark's V015a decoy.

variants.text: At inference, dropout's random deactivation is turned off; the full network is used, with activations rescaled to match training-time expectations.
DropConnect works like dropout but zeroes out individual connection weights instead of entire neuron outputs, making it a more fine-grained generalization of the dropout idea.
The original motivation for batch normalization was that it reduces internal covariate shift -- the shifting distribution of layer inputs during training.
Later research found batch normalization's real benefit is making the loss landscape smoother for optimization, not reducing internal covariate shift as originally claimed.
ResNet adds shortcut/identity connections so a block only needs to learn the residual (difference) from its input, which helps gradients flow through very deep networks.
Skip connections in ResNet let very deep networks (100+ layers) train successfully by giving gradients an unimpeded path backward.
DenseNet's dense connectivity, where every layer receives the feature maps of all preceding layers, promotes feature reuse and helps gradients reach early layers.
Full self-attention has quadratic time and memory cost in the sequence length, since every token attends to every other token.
Self-attention scales linearly with sequence length.
variants.notes: True only for sparse/linear-attention variants (M018), false for standard full self-attention. Classic dropped-exception overgeneralization, analog to physics's K004m Invar-alloy decoy.

variants.text: Restricting each token's attention to a local window or fixed pattern reduces attention's cost from quadratic to roughly linear in sequence length.
BERT is trained by masking some input tokens and predicting them using context from both directions.
GPT is trained purely to predict the next token given only the preceding tokens, never seeing future context during training.
DQN combines Q-learning with a deep neural network function approximator so it can operate directly on high-dimensional inputs like pixels.
Pruning trims individual weights or whole structural units, like channels or neurons, out of a trained network to shrink it.
